objectives: To elucidate whether probiotic oral bacteriotherapy attenuates oxidative/nitrosative stress, oxidative biomolecule damage, and inflammation in patients with non-communicable diseases.
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials in patients with non-communicable diseases characterized by inflammatory processes and oxidative stress; clearly defined probiotic intervention (single- or multi-strain) with dose and duration specified; placebo control; viable outcome data for oxidative/nitrosative stress or related inflammatory markers; adequate quantitative data (MD or SMD with SD/SE); clear diagnostic criteria; and at least three studies reporting at least one shared primary oxidative/nitrosative stress outcome.
exclusion_criteria: Studies not relevant to the topic or not reporting the clinical outcomes of interest; missing protocol or full text; non-viable primary/secondary endpoint data; non-RCTs or trials without a control group; animal or in vitro studies; non-NCD populations (including healthy, pregnant, overweight/obese participants); infectious diseases and inflammatory bowel diseases; complex chronic conditions with unclear underlying cause; probiotic interventions combined with another nutraceutical or unclear microbial composition; and active-control/placebo regimens that also contained probiotics, prebiotics, or other agents.
